annotations.text:
Inkyscib editor chrome — three directions.

The axis is where tool options live. Everything else is held constant so the comparison is fair: same eight tools, same names, same colour set, same accent (#5a5aff), your real dark/light canvas backgrounds, 44px tap targets throughout.

Each artboard has a Theme switch (dark/light) above it, and the tools are clickable — pick one and the options follow.

Options open in a detached popover under the bar.

Calmest of the three and the smallest change to ship — closest to what you already have.

Trade-off: the popover covers the canvas while it is open, and the bar runs out of width as tools are added.

Options live inside the bar itself, which grows a second row. Nothing else is on screen — no top bar at all.

Most canvas visible, thumb-reachable on a tablet, and only one surface to learn.

Trade-off: the bar changes height as you switch tools, which can feel jumpy, and the document title is buried in the dock.

Options are always visible in a panel that never opens or closes, plus page thumbnails on the right.

Fastest to work in once learned — nothing is hidden, and it suits the algebra-tiles and geometry tools that have many settings.

Trade-off: densest of the three, and it eats horizontal room on a small tablet.
